Hi Samantha —

Appreciate the clear scope. Below is the security/compliance answer in plain terms, followed by implementation specifics and mitigations we recommend:

1) What happens when live data is deleted?- We mark the record as deleted in the live datastore immediately and remove access paths so it is no longer served.

2) Backups & snapshots — timeline and behavior- Regular backups: customer backups are incremental snapshots stored encrypted in the EU region (customer-configured region for Private; hosted EU S3 for Redwood-hosted). Snapshots are retained according to the customer's retention policy (default hosted retention: 90 days).
- Deletion propagation: when a delete occurs on live data we flag corresponding entries for deletion in the next backup cycle; however, previously written snapshot objects remain immutable until their retention window expires or are garbage-collected.
- Practical timelines: removal from all backup copies typically occurs at the end of the retention window. Our nightly GC process marks expired snapshots for deletion; object-level deletion from cloud storage can take up to 72 hours after GC due to provider eventual consistency and object lifecycle transitions.

3) Expedited purge / ERASURE requests- For enterprise customers (Reserved/Dedicated and qualifying Private customers) we offer an expedited purge procedure: we run targeted snapshot rehydration + selective object rewrite to exclude the deleted customer data, then rotate encryption keys and trigger provider-side deletes. This is available under an addendum or as part of certain compliance packages. Typical SLA: 7–14 business days from approved request, depending on replication and cross-region copies.

4) Legal hold and retention overrides- If legal hold is requested, snapshots are excluded from GC until release. Our tooling surfaces holds on a per-account basis to prevent accidental purge and to document chain-of-custody.

5) Cross-region DR copies- If you enable cross-region replication for DR, replicated snapshots follow the destination region's retention and deletion behavior; an expedite in EU still requires coordination to remove copies in the other region(s). That can add latency to full eradication.

6) Key management & crypto considerations- We use per-tenant CMKs (customer-managed keys available for Private/Dedicated; Redwood-managed keys for hosted). Key rotation or deletion is a strong mitigation: destroying the key makes data computationally unrecoverable, but this is sensitive and irreversible — we only do this with explicit signed approvals.

Recommended customer controls:
- Set conservative retention windows aligned to policy (e.g., 30 days for low-risk workloads, 90+ for audit-critical).
- Use Private or Dedicated deployment if you require faster purge SLAs and full control over storage lifecycles and CMKs.
- For GDPR erasure requests that must be immediate, plan for the expedited purge addendum to reduce timelines.

I've attached the SOC2 section that describes backup verification and retention controls. Happy to walk through the runbook with your team.

— Naomi

Hi Samantha — technical follow-up on the attestations and timelines.

Attestation: Our expedited purge workflow includes an audit package:
- A summary report of steps performed (snapshots inspected, rehydration IDs, keys rotated).
- Before/after snapshot indices with checksums showing excluded objects (redacted to avoid leaking other customers' metadata).
- Ops ticket and timestamped runbook logs.
We can provide a signed attestation for legal/regulatory uses as part of the purge engagement.

Timeline differences:
- Hosted (Redwood-managed keys): expedited purge relies on snapshot-level rehydration and selective rewrite; we cannot rotate a customer CMK, so eradication depends on object deletion plus lifecycle — typical expedited SLA ~10–14 business days once approved.
- Dedicated/Private (Customer-managed CMK): if you control the CMK, you can request key destruction after the data rehydration/removal step; destroying the key makes prior encrypted objects irrecoverable immediately (subject to contractual approval). That path can reduce effective eradication to 2–7 business days because it avoids waiting for provider lifecycle windows, but it requires coordination and explicit acceptance of the irreversibility.

Operational notes:
- Backup GC runs nightly and marks expired segments. Cross-region replication TTLs are evaluated before deletion; we include replication verification in the purge procedure.
- For very short retention needs (e.g., <30 days) we recommend Dedicated with retention policies tuned and CMKs for the fastest compliance posture.

If you like, we can scope an expedited purge addendum and include an attestation template for your legal team to review.

— Rishi
